name: Marinahua
confidence_why: Pike & Scott 1962 place the prominent (lengthened) syllable on the first syllable of the stem in Peruvian Marinahua-Sharanahua and Scott 2004, from the same fieldwork, treats disyllables as accented on the first syllable, while the fixed final stress of Souza 2005 and 2012 and the free stress of Cunha 1993 describe the Brazilian Arara-Shawãdawa varieties filed under the same code, not the variety of the record.
catalog_citation: Pike, Eunice V. & Eugene Scott. 1962. The phonological hierarchy of Marinahua. Phonetica 8: 1-8. (archive.org item rosettaproject_mcd_phon-1, 'Sharanahua Phonology'; scanned text + PDF saved)
catalog_locator: Sec. 2 'The phonological word', pp. 2-3; Sec. 3 'Phonological clause', p. 4; Sec. 9 'Tone contrasts', p. 7
catalog_quote: Each phonological word is a rhythm unit with a nuclear syllable which is longer than other syllables of that word. When a phonological word is the last one in the phonological clause, the nuclear syllable is even longer. The nuclear syllable of the phonological word corresponds to the first syllable of a stem of a grammatical word. It is, therefore, usually the first syllable of the phonological word. When it is not initial in the phonological word, it has been indicated by a raised dot: nata-ri these clothes (na this, tari clothes). The syllable at the end of a phonological word is shorter and more lenis than a prenuclear or nuclear syllable. ... In the examples, unless the word contains a raised dot, the first syllable after space is the nuclear syllable and is, therefore, lengthened ... [Sec. 9] Each emic syllable has either a high or a low tone. Note the following words: pia nephew,…

tone_statements.citation: González, Carolina. 2017. Tipología de los sistemas métricos de veinticinco lenguas Pano. Amerindia 39(1): 129-172. (In: P. Valenzuela & A. Guillaume (eds.), Estudios sincrónicos y diacrónicos sobre lenguas Pano y Takana: fonología, morfología y sintaxis.)
tone_statements.quote: Una situación similar se da en sharanawa (marinahua), donde la sílaba acentuada es la primera de la raíz. Esta sílaba es más larga que otras en la palabra; en cambio, la sílaba final es más corta y débil que una acentuada o pre-acentuada (Pike & Scott 1962: 2; ver también Shell 1975: 39, nota a pie de página 25). [...] Es posible que en otras lenguas cuya acentuación ha sido poco estudiada, como el yaminahua y el sharanawa, haya una distinción similar entre la asignación acentual y tonal.
tone_statements.translation: A similar situation obtains in Sharanawa (Marinahua), where the stressed syllable is the first syllable of the root. This syllable is longer than the others in the word; the final syllable, by contrast, is shorter and weaker than a stressed or pre-stressed one (Pike & Scott 1962: 2; see also Shell 1975: 39, footnote 25). [...] It is possible that in other languages whose accentuation has been little studied, such as Yaminahua and Sharanawa, there is a similar distinction between stress assignment and tone assignment.
tone_statements.locator: sec. 4 'Lenguas trocaicas', p. 151 for the Sharanawa passage; sec. 7 'Discusión', p. 164 for the accent/tone remark; Table 1 p. 133; Shawã sec. 3.2.2 pp. 145-147; Arara sec. 6 p. 161

En las palabras de dos sílabas las secuencias ~e tono son alto como en /fáí/ 'sendero•, bajo bajo como en /fai/.~camp6, . jardín•, alto bajo corno en /fái/ 'creciente del rÍu'. Un radical de dos sílabas con la secuencia tonal de bajo alto no se ha hallado en forma aislada
tone_statements.translation: In M[arinahua], tone is phonemic, each syllable having a high tone or a low tone [fn. 36: according to Scott and Pike, p. 1ff.]. There are one-syllable words whose tone is high and others whose tone is low, e.g. /cí/ 'fire', /rto/ 'chigoe flea'. In two-syllable words the tone sequences are high[-high] as in /fáí/ 'path', low-low as in /fai/ 'field, garden', high-low as in /fái/ 'rising of the river'. A two-syllable root with the tonal sequence low-high has not been found in isolation form.
tone_statements.locator: pp. 51-52, capítulo 2 'Sistemas fonémicos' (prosody survey, paragraph beginning 'En el M, el tono es fonémico', with fn. 36 'según Scott y Pike'); see also fn. 25, p. 39

audit.recode_to: no reclassification for Marinahua. Scope the record explicitly to the Peruvian Marinahua/Sharanahua dialect (mari1443) and add a caution: the Brazilian Shawãdawa/Arara dialect that Glottolog places under the same glottocode (shaw1250) is described with fixed final stress and no tone (Souza 2005:74; 2012:25-27) or free accent (Cunha 1993 sec. 1.4); if the catalog must carry one value per glottocode, flag shar1245 as dialect-divergent rather than 'morphological' tout court.
audit.reasoning: (1) Quote check: the deciding quotation, domain quote and exceptions quote are verbatim in the held archive.org scanned text of Pike & Scott 1962 at the stated sections/pages (Sec. 2 pp. 2-3, Sec. 3 p. 4, Sec. 9 p. 7); the 12 Sep the compilers had already cross-checked the PDF text. (2) Deciding source: a 1962 Phonetica phonology article by Eunice Pike (SIL's tone specialist) and the resident fieldworker; short and non-instrumental, but Glottolog's full 57-item bibliography for shar1245 (downloaded via langdoc JSON) contains no later phonology or grammar of the Peruvian variety — only Scott & Frantz 1974 (questions), Loos 1975 (nasalization, 4 pp.), Scott 1979 texts, Scott 2004 dictionary, Anonby 2022 sociolinguistic survey, Déléage ethnography. sources.citation: Souza, Emerson Carvalho de. 2012. Aspectos de uma gramática Shawã (Pano). Tese de doutorado, Universidade Estadual de Campinas (IEL). xxiii+153 pp. (etnolinguistica.org tese:souza-2012)
sources.quote: p. 26: 'independentemente do número de sílabas de que a palavra é constituída, o acento é sempre regular, caindo de forma recorrente na última sílaba. Os dados em (24: i-m) ainda nos mostram que mesmo com acréscimo de afixos, o acento permanece recaindo na sílaba final' ([kaˈma] 'cachorro', [utuˈku] 'macaco', [kutavaisˈti]); analysed as unbounded iambs with glottal-stop epenthesis on a light final stressed syllable ('Iambic Lengthening'); p. 122: 'o Shawã se enquadra no grupo de línguas ... portadoras de acento fixo ... o acento sempre se localiza sobre a última sílaba das palavras'. No lexica
sources.locator: sec. 4.7 'O acento na língua Shawã', pp. 25-27; p. 49; Conclusão p. 122
sources.note: Only modern grammar under glottocode shar1245 with a dedicated stress section; describes the Brazilian Shawãdawa dialect (shaw1250) as fixed: final syllable stress with no tone, opposite edge to our Marinahua stem-initial coding — needed to scope the record to the Peruvian dialect or split it.

sources.citation: Cunha, Carla Maria. 1993. A morfossintaxe da língua Arara (Pano) do Acre. Dissertação de mestrado, Universidade Federal de Pernambuco, Recife. x+174 pp. (etnolinguistica.org tese:cunha-1993)
sources.quote: 'A acentuação, na língua Arara, é livre e sua ocorrência não se dá fixamente em uma determinada sílaba. ... A língua Arara, mesmo em palavras dissílabas e pronunciadas isoladamente, não tem preferência por uma acentuação na última sílaba, ela varia constantemente: [aˈda] língua, [ˈasoa] boca, [ˈkama] cachorro, [takaˈra] galinha, [vaˈka] água, [ˈvaka ˈkaya] água do rio'. Contrasts Katukina's fixed final accent (Barros 1987). No tone analysis. Variety: Arara (Shawãdawa), Igarapé Humaitá, Cruzeiro do Sul, Acre.
sources.locator: cap. I sec. 1.4 'Acento', p. 95ff (TOC); Introdução ('acentuação livre')
sources.note: Glottolog's top-ranked 'grammar' for shar1245; sec. 1.4 says Arara (Shawãdawa) accent is free/variable ([ˈkama] ~ [vaˈka]) — a third, different statement for the Brazilian dialect; low analytic depth but documents the within-glottocode disagreement.

sources.quote: p. 74: '[vaˈkaʔ] água ... [bitʃkaˈti] pedra ... nossos exemplos evidenciam que nessa língua, exceto os monossilábicos, o acento recai sempre sobre a última sílaba da palavra simples. Trata-se, então, de uma manifestação predizível ... não é fonêmico'; p. 75: 'sua ocorrência é previsível, pois se manifesta sempre na última sílaba da palavra'. Variety: Jamináwa-Arara, rio Bagé, Marechal Thaumaturgo, Acre, Brazil (Glottolog files this under shar1245).
sources.locator: sec. 3.5.1 'O acento em item lexical simples', p. 74; Conclusão p. 75
sources.note: Glottolog's only other 'phonology' item for shar1245; states predictable word-final accent for the Jamináwa-Arara variety (p. 74) — second Brazilian witness against generalising the Marinahua rule to the whole languoid.
